filter-chip-group.purpose: Expose active filters as removable chips with reset, count, overflow, keyboard behavior, and empty recovery.
useWhen: Users need to review and remove active filters quickly.
Filters are applied outside the current viewport or from multiple controls.
A query needs clear count, reset, and empty state feedback.
doNotUseWithoutReview: There are no active filters to review.
Removing filters has unclear persistence or side effects.
The chips become the only way to discover available filters.
foundations: Defines chip wrapping, overflow, reset placement, and compact behavior.
Owns filter labels, count copy, reset label, and empty copy.
Controls selected, removable, disabled, and focus states.
Empty, active, overflow, dirty, applied, and cleared states are explicit.
Requires removable button semantics and count feedback.
slots: Shown when no filters are active.
variants: Removable chips with count and clear action.
Excess filters collapse or wrap with clear count.
motion: Chip disappears without moving keyboard focus unpredictably.
Empty state replaces chips after user action.
accessibility: Empty state is announced when all filters are cleared.
tests: Clear all hides chips and shows Empty State.

canDecide: Use Filter Chip Group for active filters already applied.
Show Empty State when all filters are removed.
mustAsk: Filter persistence, query side effects, or reset behavior is unclear.
rejectIf: Chips are static labels with no removal behavior.
miel.handoff: Confirm filter source, removal behavior, reset policy, count copy, and empty state.
